一: A single, horizontal line is all you need to represent the number **one**.
二: Just like the Roman numeral, **two** parallel lines represent the number **two**.
九: Imagine a fishhook with a long line, ready to catch **nine** fish.
七: It looks like a capital 'T' with an extra diagonal stroke, hinting at the lucky number **seven**.
人: This kanji looks like a **person** walking, with two legs striding forward.
入: Imagine a person's legs pointing inward, as they **enter** a room.
八: The two strokes diverge like a pair of chopsticks opening up to pick up **eight** pieces of food.
十: It's a cross, like when you add up all your fingers and toes to get **ten**.
三: Three horizontal lines stacked on top of each other clearly represent the number **three**.
上: The short stroke is **above** the long ground line, connected by a vertical line showing direction.
下: The short stroke is **below** the long ground line, connected by a vertical line showing direction.
大: A **large** person stands with their arms and legs spread wide, showing their great size.
女: This kanji depicts a **woman** sitting gracefully, perhaps with her arms folded or legs crossed.
山: It clearly resembles three majestic peaks of a **mountain** range.
川: Three flowing lines represent the gentle current of a **stream** or river.
土: A plant (vertical line) grows out of the **soil** (bottom line), with a little dirt clump (top line) on top.
千: Imagine a cross for ten, and a little extra stroke makes it a **thousand** times bigger!
子: This kanji looks like a little **child** with a big head and small, outstretched arms.
小: Three tiny dots falling down, representing something very **little** or small.
中: A stick plunged right through the **middle** of a square, showing it's **in** something.
五: Imagine a tally mark for five, where the last stroke dramatically crosses the first four to complete the count.
六: A **lid** (亠) on top of two **fins** (八) suggests a fish that's number six in a race, barely covered.
円: A **lid** (亠) rests perfectly on a **head** (口) creating a smooth, round **circle**.
天: A person (大) stretches their arms wide, reaching up to touch the very top bar of the **heavens**.
日: This kanji clearly depicts the radiant **sun** (日) itself, a bright rectangle with a line across, shining down on the **day**.
月: This kanji looks like a slender crescent **moon** (月) in the night sky, marking the passage of a **month**.
木: Visualize a sturdy **tree** (木) with its trunk, branches, and roots firmly planted.
水: Imagine three streams of **water** (水) flowing downwards, with a central strong current and two smaller rivulets on the sides.
火: This kanji resembles a flickering **fire** (火), with two flames rising from a central burning ember.
出: Two mountains (山) are stacked on top of each other, forming a narrow passage to **exit** a valley.
右: A **mouth** (口) is held in the **right** hand (又), perhaps to whisper a secret or enjoy a snack.
四: Imagine a box (口) with a cross inside, neatly dividing it into **four** equal sections.
左: The **left** hand (又) holds a carpenter's square (工), ready to begin **construction**.
本: A **tree** (木) with an extra line at its base, pointing to its **root** or origin, which is like the fundamental knowledge found in a **book**.
白: The **sun** (日) shines so intensely that it makes everything appear pure **white** (白), with a single drop of light escaping.
万: Imagine a single, powerful stroke (一) cutting through the air like a sword (刀), signifying a vast quantity, like **ten thousand**.
今: A person (人, slightly altered) is speaking **now** from their **mouth** (口).
午: Visualize a clock hand pointing straight up at **noon** (午), dividing the day perfectly in half.
友: Two hands (又, a common component for hand) are clasped together, symbolizing two **friends** (友) united.
父: This kanji looks like a **father** (父) with broad shoulders and outstretched arms, ready to embrace his child.
北: Two people (represented by the two 'spoons' or 'fingers' 匕) have turned their backs on each other and are heading North, away from each other.
半: A single triceratops horn (top part) cuts a dry field (bottom part) right in half, splitting it perfectly.
外: In the evening (夕), you put your toe (卜) outside to test the temperature before venturing out.
母: This kanji clearly depicts a Mother with two breasts (the two dots) ready to nurse her child.
休: A person (人, the 'leader') leaning against a tree (木) to rest.
先: A person with legs (儿) leads the way, sliding (like a slide over dirt) before anyone else.
名: In the evening (夕), you use your mouth (口) to whisper your secret name.
年: Every year, the farmer uses a gun (干) to protect his cow (牛, whose lower part resembles the bottom of 年).
気: The vital spirit (気) is like energy (气, steam) rising, a precious treasure (乂, the cross can be seen as a treasure mark) within.
百: Imagine a single leaf (一, the top stroke) falling onto the sun (日, part of 白), representing one out of a hundred such leaves.
男: A **male** works hard in the **rice paddy**, showing his **power**.
見: An **eye** with little **legs** has gone out to **see** the world.
車: This kanji looks like a bird's-eye view of a **car**, with the top box being the cabin and the lines representing wheels or axles.
毎: **Every** single time, a tiny **gun** (匕) pops out of the **window** (口) to announce its presence.
行: This kanji looks like two people **going** for a walk together, or two legs striding forward.
西: The kanji for **West** looks like a covered wagon with a roof and wheels, heading **west** into the sunset.
何: **What** is that **leader** doing with a **lip ring**?
来: The **rice** has **come** up from the **ground**, ready for harvest.
学: A **child** under a big **Viking** helmet is diligently trying to **study**.
金: This kanji looks like a strong central pillar of wealth supporting two nuggets of **gold** on top and two more below.
雨: Imagine a cloud at the top with four drops of rain falling down, just like the kanji's shape.
国: A king (王) with a single jewel (、) rules over his entire country (口), enclosed by its borders.
東: The sun (日) is rising just behind a large tree (木), illuminating the east.
長: This kanji depicts a long-haired elder with a long beard, symbolizing something that is long or a leader.
前: Imagine a boat (舟, simplified) with its sail (top part) and a crescent moon (月) appearing right in front of it on the horizon.
南: A cross (十) marks the spot for sheep (羊, top part of sheep) that are heading south for warmer pastures.
後: You're walking (彳) slowly, a small (幺) child trailing behind you, trying to catch up in the cold winter (夂).
食: The lid (人) is lifted from a bowl (良) of food, revealing a mouth (口) ready to eat.
校: At a school with many trees (木), a strict father (父) makes you cross (乂) off answers during a difficult exam.
時: The sun (日) marks the passage of time, much like the bells of a temple (寺) mark the hours.
高: Imagine a *tall* building with a fancy "lid" on top, many "mouths" (windows) on its side, and a decorative "mustache" balcony making it even *taller*.
間: The "sun" peeking through a "gate" marks the *interval* of the day, or the *interval* of time you wait for someone to pass through.
話: To tell a *tale*, you must "say" (言) it with your "tongue" (舌), letting your words flow.
電: *Electricity* often comes with "rain" and lightning, illuminating the "rice paddies." The zigzag line under the "rain" looks like a lightning bolt.
聞: You put your "ear" right up to the "gate" to *hear* what secrets are being whispered inside.
語: When you "say" a *word*, it's like speaking "five" times from your "mouth" to make it clear.
読: When you *read*, you might "say" the words out loud, perhaps to "sell" the story to an audience.
生: This kanji looks like a small plant sprouting from the ground, symbolizing new *life* emerging.
書: To *write* well, you need a good "brush" and plenty of light from the "sun" to see what you're doing.
力: This kanji looks like a flexing arm, showing off its *power* and strength.
口: This kanji looks exactly like an open mouth!
工: Imagine a craftsman using a T-square or working at a workbench to create something with their craft.
夕: This kanji looks like a sliver of the moon just appearing in the sky, signaling the evening is beginning.
手: This character looks like a stylized drawing of a hand, with the three 'fingers' at the top and the 'wrist' at the bottom.
文: Think of a person (大) with their legs crossed, carefully writing out a beautiful sentence or a piece of literature.
犬: This kanji looks like a happy dog wagging its tail, with the little dot being its head.
正: To do something correctly, you must stop (止) and stand firm on the ground (一).
田: This kanji clearly depicts a bird's-eye view of a rice field divided into plots for cultivation.
目: This kanji looks just like an eye with a pupil and iris, looking out at the world.
立: This kanji shows a person (大) standing up firmly on the ground (一), ready to go.
元: The top stroke is the head, the very *beginning* or origin of a person.
公: What is shared by *eight* (八) people becomes *public*, no longer *private* (ム).
切: Use a *sword* (刀) to *cut* something into *seven* (七) pieces.
少: It looks like 'small' (小), but with an extra flick, representing just a *few* tiny drops, even less than small.
心: This kanji visually represents the chambers and valves of a human *heart*.
方: Picture a flag on a pole, pointing in a specific *direction*.
牛: This kanji clearly resembles the head of a *cow* with its prominent horns.
止: Picture a foot stepping down firmly, signaling to *stop* right there.
兄: Your *elder brother* (兄) is the one who stands tall (儿) and talks (口) to you.
冬: In *winter*, people bundle up (top two strokes) and walk slowly (夂) through the snow.
古: A story told by ten different mouths over time becomes very old.
台: A private (厶) item is placed on a pedestal that stands on a mouth-like base (口).
広: A canopy (广) stretches out wide to cover a private (厶) area.
用: This kanji looks like a box or tool you can utilize, with a handle on top and a slot in the middle.
世: Three horizontal lines represent three distinct generations connected by the continuous flow of time.
主: The single dot on top represents the Lord or master, standing above all, like a candle flame on its stand.
代: A person (人) is sent as a substitute to perform a task, holding a ceremonial arrow (弋) of authority.
写: Under a roof (宀), a scribe makes a copy to give (与) to someone.
去: Someone has gone from their private (厶) space, leaving only dirt (土) behind.
字: A child (子) learns to write characters under the roof (宀) of their home.
早: The sun (日) rises early, just above the horizon, looking like a cross (十) in the morning sky.
町: A town (町) is where many rice paddies (田) meet at the street boundaries (丁).
花: From the grass (艹) a tiny spoon (匕) helps a person (人) change (化) into a beautiful flower.
赤: Imagine a person (人) standing on the earth (土) getting so sunburnt they turn completely red.
足: Your leg (足) has a foot that can stop (止) you in your tracks, and sometimes it feels like it has a mouth (口) of its own.
不: The single horizontal stroke (一) means "no" or "not", blocking the person (人) below it. It's a negative sign.
仕: A person (亻) is ready to attend to the needs of the samurai (士).
会: Two people (人) meet under one roof to have a meeting.
同: Two things are the same (同) if they can both fit perfectly into the same mouth (口) or box, sharing the same ground (一).
多: When many (多) evenings (夕) have passed, you know a lot of time has gone by.
考: To deeply **consider** something, one might contemplate the stark reality of a beggar (乞) resting on a coffin (老's top part).
肉: This kanji looks like a cross-section of muscle fibers, clearly showing a slab of **meat** ready to be eaten.
自: It looks like a nose, which is what you point to when referring to **oneself**.
色: Imagine a person (top part) with their knees bent (bottom part), admiring the beautiful **color** of a sunset.
体: The **body** of a person (人) is like a book (本), full of stories and complex systems.
作: A person (人) uses a key (乍) to **make** or create something new.
図: This kanji is a box (口) containing a detailed **map** that shows where the treasure (貝) is located.
売: A samurai (士) stands on their legs (儿) at the market, trying to **sell** their goods.
弟: Your **younger brother** might play with a toy bow (弓) and arrow (丨), perhaps even with little 'horns' (丷) on his head.
社: A **company** is built on the dirt (土) of the land, and its spirit (示) is what drives it forward.
言: Imagine a mouth with a tongue sticking out, clearly *saying* words or making a statement.
走: Visualize a person's head and arms above two long, powerful legs *running* at full speed.
近: You take your *scooter* to get *near* the giant *axe* that fell from the sky.
空: Under the *roof* of a building, all the *construction* workers (represented by 'legs' walking away) have left, leaving the space completely *empty*.
青: Picture a plant sprout pushing through the soil towards the *blue* sky, signifying growth and vibrant color.
音: When the *sun* rises, the rooster *stands* on the fence and makes a loud *sound*.
地: An *alligator* burrows deep into the *dirt* beneath the *ground*.
安: A *woman* feels safe and can *relax* under the shelter of a *roof*.
有: A *narwhal* swimming under the *moon* would *possess* a truly magical night.
死: The *Yakuza* boss used a tiny *spoon* to finish off his victim, bringing about their *death*.
京: Under a grand LID, a small MOUTH (gate) leads into the bustling CAPITAL city.
夜: The LID of darkness descends, and the LEADER of the pack emerges, as if it's always WINTER at NIGHT.
妹: A WOMAN who is still a small, undeveloped 'JET' (未, 'not yet') is your YOUNGER SISTER.
姉: A WOMAN who is as established and important as a CITY is your ELDER SISTER.
店: Under a CANOPY, you visit a STORE hoping to find good FORTUNE.
明: When the SUN and MOON both shine, it creates a BRIGHT light.
歩: To WALK, you STOP, take a SMALL step, then move forward (slide).
画: With a BRUSH-STROKE, you draw a picture of a RICE PADDY inside a BOX.
知: When you KNOW something, the answer comes out of your MOUTH as direct as an ARROW.
室: Under a ROOF, you ARRIVE at your private ROOM.
思: Your heart works hard like a farmer in a rice paddy when you think deeply.
海: A tsunami of water from the sea crashes so hard it sounds like a gun shot, visible from your window.
茶: To make tea, you pick flowers (leaves) from a plant, and it's so good it feels like an angel wearing a hat is serving it to you.
以: By means of a single drop of effort, a person can grow strong like a lion.
夏: In summer, with your eye you see green leaves, a stark contrast to the slow pace of winter.
家: Under the roof of a house, a pig was traditionally kept for sustenance.
紙: Paper is made from pressed thread fibers, historically used to record the lineage of a clan.
通: Traffic moves along a path (scooter radical) where a mama is always busy with a task.
強: To be strong, you need to master your bow and arrow, even if your private target is just a tiny insect.
教: A patient teacher will teach you lessons that help you grow, even through the long, cold days of winter.
